import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    # Create a dummy dataframe for execution if the file doesn't exist
    print("Warning: 'data/cameras.csv' not found. Generating dummy data for visualization.")
    np.random.seed(42)
    brands = ['Canon', 'Nikon', 'Sony', 'Fuji', 'Leica', 'Pentax', 'Olympus']
    sensor_types = ['Full Frame', 'APS-C', 'Micro 4/3', 'Medium Format']
    body_types = ['DSLR', 'Mirrorless', 'Compact']
    data = {
        'brand': np.random.choice(brands, 1000),
        'model_year': np.random.randint(2005, 2024, 1000),
        'megapixels': np.random.uniform(12, 65, 1000),
        'max_iso': np.random.choice([12800, 25600, 51200, 102400, 204800], 1000),
        'weight_grams': np.random.randint(200, 1500, 1000),
        'price_usd': np.clip(np.random.lognormal(mean=7.5, sigma=0.8, size=1000), 200, 8000),
        'sensor_type': np.random.choice(sensor_types, 1000, p=[0.3, 0.45, 0.2, 0.05]),
        'has_video_4k': np.random.randint(0, 2, 1000),
        'lens_mount': 'Generic',
        'body_type': np.random.choice(body_types, 1000)
    }
    df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="muted")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the scatter plot (bubble chart)
# This chart shows the relationship between Price and Megapixels,
# while also encoding Sensor Type (color) and Weight (size)
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='weight_grams',
    sizes=(30, 600),
    alpha=0.7,
    palette='viridis',
    ax=ax,
    edgecolor="black",
    linewidth=0.5,
    hue_order=sorted(df['sensor_type'].unique()) # Ensure consistent legend order
)

# Set plot title and labels with enhanced formatting
ax.set_title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type and Weight', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Format the y-axis to display as currency
formatter = mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${int(x):,}')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)

# Improve the legend by splitting it into two separate legends for clarity
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()

# Find the start of the size legend entries
try:
    size_legend_start_index = labels.index('weight_grams') + 1
    # Create the color (hue) legend
    color_handles = handles[1:size_legend_start_index-1]
    color_labels = labels[1:size_legend_start_index-1]
    color_legend = ax.legend(color_handles, color_labels,
                             title='Sensor Type',
                             title_fontsize='13',
                             fontsize='11',
                             loc='upper left',
                             bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
                             borderaxespad=0.)
    ax.add_artist(color_legend) # Add the color legend back to the plot

    # Create the size legend
    size_handles = handles[size_legend_start_index:]
    size_labels = labels[size_legend_start_index:]
    size_legend = ax.legend(size_handles, size_labels,
                            title='Weight (grams)',
                            title_fontsize='13',
                            fontsize='11',
                            loc='lower left',
                            bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0),
                            borderaxespad=0.)
except ValueError:
    # Fallback for cases where the legend structure is simpler
    ax.legend(title='Legend', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
